doc.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999

title: Joe Glaser's call and the pitch to join Louis
summary: Marty refused at first because of his vow to his wife; Red Norvo urged him on and he accepted.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Oh well I don’t mean especially Red Norvo. He came to mind because he’s the reason why I went with Louis. Not especially but when Joe Glaser called me, the first time he called me to go with Louis, it’s a funny story because he said, “Marty this is Joe Glaser. Did you work with Phil Napoleon’s Memphis Five?” I said, “yeah, why?” He said, “you play Dixieland?” I said, “I guess so, if I worked with Phil’s band I guess.” He said, “well you want to go with Louis Armstrong?” And I said, “no.” He said, “did you hear what I said?” I said, “yeah, Louis Armstrong.” He says, “you don’t want to go with Louis?” I said, “no.” Because of the fact that I had just left a group, now I didn’t leave the group it broke up, I was with a quartet just before I went with Louis. I worked with Phil Napoleon then I went with a group called The Big Four. And we went to Chicago for two weeks and we stayed four months. And my wife was up to here. She said, “I’m going to leave you.” Finally what happened was the group broke up and we came back to New York and that’s when Joe Glaser called me. And I said, “No I can’t Mr. Glaser.” He says, “Why?” I said, well “You booked The Big Four.” He was our manager/agent. And I said we were in Chicago for so long and my wife couldn’t make it anymore. So I promised my wife when the group broke up I said no more road, honey. I made a vow to my wife, no more road. Because she said it’s either me or the road. I said I prefer you so I’m home. So he says why don’t you do this, why don’t you come up and talk to me and we’ll what happens.” So I said, “Honey, I’ve got to go up and talk to him because I know Glaser for many years, he’s a nice guy —. you never know maybe he’ll get me a job someplace else to do whatever.” So I went up to see him and Red Norvo was waiting to see him. He says, “What are you doing, Marty?” I said, “Glaser called me and wanted me to go with Louis’ band.” He says, “Great.” I says, “Yeah but I don’t want to go.” He says, “What do you mean? You don’t want to go with Louis?” So I told him what happened. I said I was with

The Big Four. We went to Chicago for two weeks and we stayed four months and my wife was ready to jump off a bridge. And so was I, I mean I was away so long. So I made a promise to her I said okay that’s it, I’m not going on the road anymore. So he says, “Are you crazy?” He said, “look at what happened with Earl Hines.” Earl had a big name but not as big as Louis. But when he went with Louis, they were equal and he was getting like equal publicity and stuff. Even though Louis was the boss, but Earl, it got him exposure, and then after a while he split and got his own group, now he’s doing very well, he’s going all over the world with his own group. And I’m listening to him like a jerk — not like a jerk because I went in and by the time I went inside Glaser said —. I says, “well okay.”
Ooh. That must have been a long trip home.
Well of course I called my wife and said, “honey, guess what?” And she said, “You’re kidding.” She’s been through, I’ll tell you she’s gone through a lot with me, really. She’s been through a lot.
